advice: Use a cache-blocked scalar C fallback with small fixed row and column tiles and an increasing-k inner loop. Initialize each C tile to zero, then iterate k blocks in ascending order and update C[i:i+MR, j:j+NR] using FP32 multiply-adds. Keep a scalar cleanup path for incomplete tiles. Add checked size arithmetic for any scratch allocation; the fallback itself can avoid allocation entirely. Route only unsupported-SME or allocation-failure cases to this path, while preserving n<=0 as an immediate return. This is a general C change: it improves B and C locality for edge shapes without relying on the benchmark size, external libraries, or input values.
risks: No portable tile size is established by the supplied evidence, and compiler vectorization may change rounding or fail to vectorize the intended loops. Do not claim a speedup. Ensure the accumulation order remains increasing in k and check the existing 0.002 relative-to-reference maximum error on odd and small sizes, plus n<=0. Check unsupported-SME dispatch and allocation-failure behavior. Any performance decision needs the specified repeated paired measurements against a fresh AC baseline.
